chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), that he was asked:

About the man who contracts for the work, then does not work in it himself, and hands it over to another, so he profits from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless it so happened that he had done some work in it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sub-contracting work if the contractor does no work themselves?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of *al-mu'awana* (sub-contracting) by establishing that mere delegation without personal contribution renders the contract void, a principle distinguishing it from valid profit-sharing arrangements. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on active participation and effort (*ijtihad*) as a prerequisite for legitimate ownership of the resulting profit, preventing unjust enrichment through pure intermediation.
